{"question": "What does TIMEOUT_CYCLES do?", "proposed_default": "It is the shell host-link timeout only; the screener never ends a packet on idle time"}
{"question": "What are the values of CLKS_PER_BIT, TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?", "proposed_default": "868, 1000000, 0"}

reply.answer: CLKS_PER_BIT is 868, which matches the proposed default. TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not the proposed 1000000. BUILD_STAMP is not specified.

question: {"question": "Should not-new keep separate counters for repeat and out-of-order?", "proposed_default": "No, one not-new counter covers both"}

reply.answer: Yes. The specification gives repeat and stale their own counters, 0x14 for repeat and 0x15 for stale. The proposed single not-new counter is not in the spec.
reply.quote: Counters 0x10 good, 0x11 bad check, 0x12 short, 0x13 long, 0x14 repeat, 0x15 stale, 0x16 protocol (type and length), 16-bit wrapping.

question: {"question": "What is the numeric code of each class in the result register?", "proposed_default": "0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length"}

reply.answer: Yes. The RESULT register codes are: 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length.
reply.quote: RESULT: offset 0x01, RO, reset 0: class of the last packet: 0 none, 1 good, 2 bad check, 3 short, 4 long, 5 repeat, 6 stale, 7 bad type, 8 bad length
